transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. I guess… work is why I’m here. I’m a cashier, and lately at the register I keep getting stuck doing things that don’t really make sense right then. Like I’ll tap the scanner in a certain pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting.

It’s embarrassing, because the line backs up, and people look at you like you’re doing it on purpose. Last week they wrote me up for it. I used to be pretty good with customers, you know, I have my own way of bagging things—cans with cans, cold stuff separate—but this is different. I don’t know, I just get caught in it.
When you get stuck tapping or freezing, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve a bad thought or anxiety?

I don’t know if it’s exactly to relieve anxiety. It’s more like… I’m at the register and my hand just gets stuck in the wrong thing, like tapping the scanner in a pattern when I should be scanning, or I freeze over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting.

And then the line builds up, and that makes me nervous after, because people stare. It reminds me of when the card machine used to jam all the time—everybody thinks it’s your fault, even if it isn’t. But this time it’s me doing it, I guess. Last week they wrote me up for it.
Right before you tap or freeze, do you get an unwanted thought or urge that feels like you have to act on it?

It’s not like there’s a thought first, exactly. I don’t think, “Oh, I have to tap or something bad happens.” It’s more… I’m just at the register and suddenly I’m doing the wrong thing for the moment. Like tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand is over the cash drawer and I just stop there, even though the customer is waiting.

And then it turns into a whole thing, because the line gets backed up, and people get impatient. I’ve worked registers a long time, so I know how it’s supposed to go. But last week it happened enough that they wrote me up.
When the tapping or freezing happens, does it feel involuntary, like your body does it on its own?

Yeah… kind of. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it, not in the normal way. I’ll be at the register and I know the customer is there, I know I’m supposed to scan or open the drawer, but then I’m tapping the scanner in this little pattern or my hand just stops over the cash drawer.

It’s weird because I can see it happening, like when you drop a coin and watch it roll under something, and you’re just standing there. I used to have this whole rhythm at work, bags lined up right and everything, and now it’s like I get stuck in the wrong part of the motion. Last week they wrote me up for it, so… yeah, it feels like my body gets ahead of me or doesn’t listen for a minute.
Right before the tapping or freezing happens, do you feel a buildup in your body that gets better only after you do it?

I don’t really notice a buildup, like pressure in my chest or something that goes away after. It’s not like that, I don’t think.

It’s more that I’m at the register and I just… get caught doing the wrong thing. Tapping the scanner in this pattern when I’m supposed to be ringing someone up, or my hand just stays over the cash drawer while they’re waiting. Then I realize the line is getting longer, and that’s when I get tense. I came in because it’s been happening enough that last week they wrote me up, and I can’t afford that.
If you really try, can you hold back the tapping or freezing for a little while?

I mean, I try to, yeah. I tell myself, just finish the sale, scan the item, open the drawer, normal stuff. But then I’m standing there and it’s like I’m already tapping the scanner, or my hand is just hanging there over the cash drawer while the customer’s looking at me.

Sometimes I can sort of pull myself back after a second, but it’s not like holding your breath or waiting out a sneeze. It just happens at the wrong time. I came in because it’s been messing up work — the line backs up, people get irritated, and last week they wrote me up for it. I’ve been a cashier a long time, so it’s embarrassing, you know.
Since you were a child, have you usually found it hard to read other people socially?

I don’t know… since I was a child is hard to say. I mean, I wasn’t the most popular kid or anything, but that was a long time ago. Kids are strange anyway, you know? One year everybody was into baseball cards, then suddenly if you had the wrong shoes it meant something.

Reading people socially… I guess I’m not sure what counts. Like knowing if someone’s joking, or if they’re mad? I can usually tell if a customer is annoyed, but that’s different, that’s right in front of me and they’re sighing or looking at the clock. Childhood, I’d have to think about it. I don’t really have a clear answer.
Outside of work, do you ever have sudden movements or sounds that just come out on their own?

Outside of work? I’m not sure. I mean, everybody makes little noises sometimes, right? Like you stub your toe or you clear your throat, or you tap your fingers when you’re thinking. My dad used to click his pen all through dinner and it drove my mother crazy, but that was just him.

For me, I haven’t really noticed something that just comes out on its own like that. The stuff I’m worried about is mostly when I’m at the register, because that’s where people are waiting and watching. At home, if I move weird or make a sound, I don’t know that I’d even catch it.
When the tapping or freezing happens, does it feel senseless and unwanted to you?

Yeah… unwanted, definitely. Senseless, I guess so, because it doesn’t match what I’m supposed to be doing. Like I’ll be at the register and instead of just scanning the item, I’m tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand is just stuck over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting.

It’s not like I think, “Oh, this is a good time to do that.” It just happens, and then I’m embarrassed because the line starts backing up. People get annoyed. Last week they wrote me up over it, which… I’ve worked as a cashier a long time, so that felt pretty bad.
When you tap the scanner in that pattern, does it feel like you have to do it until it feels just right?

I don’t know if it’s “just right,” exactly. It’s more like I’m at the register and my hand starts doing this pattern with the scanner, and it doesn’t fit the moment at all. The person is standing there waiting, the belt is still moving, and I know I should just scan the next thing.

Sometimes I get stuck the other way too, like my hand just freezes over the cash drawer. It’s embarrassing because it looks like I’m fooling around or not paying attention, and I’m not. I came in because it’s gotten bad enough that last week they wrote me up for it.
When your hand gets stuck like that, does it feel as if the action is incomplete until you do it in a very exact way?

I don’t know if I’d say “exact,” like there’s some perfect way it has to be done. It’s more that I get stuck doing something that just doesn’t belong right then.

Like at the register, my hand starts tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I freeze with my hand over the cash drawer, and the customer is just standing there. You can feel them waiting, you know? Like when you’re in line at the grocery store and the person ahead of you can’t find their card, everyone pretends they’re patient but they’re not.

That’s why I came in, really. It’s happening enough at work that last week I got written up for it, and I’ve been a cashier a long time, so that was… that was not good.
When you tap the scanner or hesitate at the register, is it because you feel the scanner, money, or cash drawer might be contaminated?

Contaminated? I don’t think that’s what it is. I mean, the scanner gets touched all day, sure, and money is kind of dirty if you think about it too much, but I’m not standing there thinking about germs or anything like that.

It’s more like my hand just… does the thing, or stops, and then I’m aware the customer is waiting. The cash drawer opens and it has that little tray with the bills, and I start thinking about whether I’m holding up the line, and then— well, at our store the register sticks sometimes too, so everybody thinks it’s the machine, but it’s not always the machine.

But no, not really contamination. I haven’t noticed it being about that.
When this happens, do you feel a need for things to be even, lined up, or in the right order?

Not really lined up, no. I mean, I notice if the little dividers on the belt are crooked sometimes, but everybody notices that, right? Like when someone leaves one halfway across and then your groceries get mixed in—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

It’s not about things being even or in order. It’s more that I’m at the register and I get stuck doing something that doesn’t fit what’s happening. Like I’ll tap the scanner in this pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer, and the customer is standing there waiting. That’s the part that’s been getting me in trouble. Last week they actually wrote me up for it.
When your hand pauses over the cash drawer, are you checking whether you already opened or closed it correctly?

No, I don’t think I’m checking it, like “did I open it right” or “did I close it right.” The drawer is open, or it isn’t — that part’s usually obvious.

It’s more that my hand just kind of hangs there, like it misses the next step. And then I’m thinking, the customer’s watching me, the line is waiting, and I should be giving change, not just standing there. Sometimes it’s that, or I start tapping the scanner in this little pattern instead of moving on.

That’s really why I came in. It’s happening at the register enough that last week I got written up for it, and I’ve been doing cashier work a long time, so it’s embarrassing.
Outside of these episodes at the register, do you generally see your habits of doing things a certain way as reasonable and appropriate?

I guess… I’m not sure. I don’t really walk around thinking, “this is a habit, and it’s reasonable,” you know? I’ve always had certain ways I do things, especially at work, because if you don’t have a routine on register everything gets messy fast — bags, receipts, the little coupon slips people don’t want, all that.

But if you mean whether I think it makes sense when I get stuck like that, then… I don’t know. In the moment it sort of feels like I’m just trying to get through the next step, not like I’m choosing some special way to do it. Then afterward I can tell it probably looked odd.

Outside the register, I haven’t really noticed it the same way. Or maybe I don’t pay attention to it unless someone’s standing there waiting on me.
If you don’t tap or pause that way, does it feel like something bad will happen?

No, not like… “if I don’t tap, something terrible happens.” It’s not that clear.

It’s more like I’m at the register and I just get stuck doing something that doesn’t fit the moment. Like the scanner tapping thing, or my hand just hanging over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. And then I’m aware they’re standing there, and the line is building up, and I’m supposed to be moving on.

I mean, the drawer is right there, the change is right there — it’s not a curse or anything. It’s just… I freeze, or I get caught in the pattern. That’s what got me written up last week. I’ve done cashier work a long time, so it’s not like I don’t know the job.
Do upsetting thoughts keep popping into your mind and make you feel driven to tap or pause like that?

I don’t know if I’d call them “upsetting thoughts,” exactly. I mean, I get upset because I’m standing there and the customer’s looking at me, and then I’m thinking about the line and the manager seeing it, but that’s after I’m already stuck, if that makes sense.

It’s not like a thought pops in first and tells me, “tap the scanner,” or “pause your hand.” It’s more like my attention slips onto the wrong thing. Like those scanners, some of them have that little ridge on the side, and you notice it under your finger, and then suddenly I’m doing that instead of finishing the sale. They changed the counter setup at our store a while back too, and the bags don’t sit right where they used to—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

So… no, I haven’t noticed a specific thought driving it. It just happens, and then I get worried because I know it looks bad.
When this happens, is your attention getting caught on how the scanner or drawer feels in your hand?

Maybe partly, yeah… like with the scanner, I’ll notice the way it sits in my hand and then I’m tapping it, but I don’t know if that’s the whole reason.

The main thing is I get stuck doing something that doesn’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing. I’ll be at the register and instead of finishing the sale, I’m tapping the scanner in some pattern, or I just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer’s standing there waiting. And then everything feels backed up — the line, the receipt, the bagging, all of it.

That’s why I came in, really. It got bad enough last week that I got written up at work.
Right before your hand starts tapping or gets stuck, do you feel a physical urge in that body part that builds up until the movement happens?

I don’t know that it’s a physical urge, like a pressure building in my hand or anything. It’s more that I’m at the register and I get caught doing the wrong thing for the moment.

Like I’ll be holding the scanner and then I’m tapping it in some pattern, or my hand is just sort of stuck over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. And then I’m thinking, okay, move, finish the sale, but I’m not doing it. The drawer’s open, the change is there, and the line is… you know, people start shifting around.

That’s really why I came in. It got me written up last week, and I’ve done cashier work for years, so it’s embarrassing. But no, I can’t say I notice a clear physical buildup right before it happens.
Do you usually feel your way of doing tasks has to follow your own exact method?

I don’t think it’s that I need some exact method, no. I mean, I’ve had my way of doing cashier work for years, but this isn’t like I’m insisting it has to be my system.

It’s more that I get stuck doing things that don’t fit the moment. Like I’m supposed to scan, take the cash, give change, keep the line moving, and instead I’m tapping the scanner in a pattern or just holding my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there. And then I’m aware of it, but it’s already happening.

Last week it got bad enough that they wrote me up, which is why I came in. I don’t think it’s about wanting it done my exact way. It’s more like I’m not doing the task when I’m supposed to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with autism spectrum features (Asperger syndrome) with restricted/repetitive sensorimotor behavior and attentional capture by sensory aspects of objects, rather than OCD, tic disorder, or anankastic personality. The patient describes getting stuck in repetitive patterns and freezing that are unwanted and impairing, with no clear obsessions, fear-based consequences, contamination concerns, checking rationale, 'just right' completion need, or anxiety relief pattern typical of OCD. Tic disorder is less supported because the patient denies a clear premonitory urge, suppressibility, and motor/vocal tics outside the register context. Personality-based rigidity is also less likely because the behaviors are ego-dystonic, situationally disruptive, and not endorsed as a preferred exact method.
